title: Internet of Things (IoT)
competency: Explain the Internet of Things, how it works, its advantages, limitations and applications.

keywords.def: A global computer network of interconnected networks using standardized communication protocols.
A network of physical objects ("things") with sensors, software and electronics that collect and exchange data over the Internet.
A device that detects something in its environment, such as temperature, motion or smoke, and turns it into data.

ideas.name: What the Internet of Things is

en.text: The Internet of Things (IoT) is a network of physical objects or people, called things, equipped with software, electronics, networks and sensors to collect and exchange data. It extends Internet connectivity beyond computers and smartphones to everyday devices, such as a toaster, an animal tracker or a diabetes monitor, so they can be controlled remotely and become smart through data, AI and networks. The Internet itself grew from ARPANET (1969) and is over 50 years old.

en.text: IoT brings efficiency (real-time data, fewer resources used), technical optimization (one smartphone controls many devices), convenience and improved customer experience, conservation (monitoring traffic, water, electricity and air in smart cities) and personalization (devices learn your preferences). Its limitations are security and privacy, dependence on Internet and power, complexity and integration of devices from different makers, and higher cost.

ideas.name: How IoT works: the four components

en.text: A complete IoT system has four components. Sensors or devices collect data from the environment, such as temperature, motion or smoke. Connectivity sends the data to the cloud through cellular, satellite, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or Ethernet. Data processing software checks the data, simply or with methods like computer vision. The user interface alerts the user by email, text or notification, and the user, or a predefined rule, can act on the system.

am.text: IoT አራት ክፍሎች አሉት፡ ሴንሰር/መሣሪያ፣ ትስስር፣ መረጃ ማቀናበር እና የተጠቃሚ በይነገጽ። ሥርዓቱ ተጠቃሚውን ያስጠነቅቃል ወይም በራሱ እርምጃ ይወስዳል።

paras: A phone has many sensors (camera, accelerometer), but it is more than a sensor.

screens.title: A cold-storage alert (sense → send → process → act)
steps: Sense: a temperature sensor reads 9 °C in a vaccine store.
Send: the reading goes to the cloud over the cellular network.
Process: software checks the rule "keep 2–8 °C" and finds it too warm.
Act: the manager gets an SMS; a predefined rule also switches on extra cooling.

en.text: IoT is used in many areas. Smart homes connect smoke detectors, light bulbs, appliances, locks, pet cameras and thermostats. Smart cities manage traffic, waste and water distribution. Supply chains track goods and inventory in real time. Connected health monitors patient care, heart rate, temperature and activity. Connected cars automate billing, insurance and parking. Smart outlets switch devices on or off remotely and track energy use.

notes.text: p.48: "The Internet was created in the late 1990s and is now more than 30 years old, with over 2 billion people" contradicts itself and is out of date. The lesson teaches: ARPANET 1969, TCP/IP 1983, World Wide Web 1989–1991; over 5 billion users in 2023 (about 5.4 billion, ITU).
p.49: the music-streaming example is cloud computing, not IoT. The lesson uses it as a non-example and gives smart speakers, smart bulbs and trackers as IoT examples.

p.52: "adjust the temperature in the cloud storage" is a typo for "cold storage" (twice). The paragraph after item 4 repeats item 4; "It instead of calling you" should be "Instead of calling you"; Figure 2.30 "User Inteface" should be "User Interface".

Table 2.1 and Review II(b): "Tacking heart rate" should be "Tracking heart rate". Activity 2.5 Q1 is garbled; read it as "Discuss routine activities at home that can be supported, managed or replaced by smart home IoT applications."
The Internet history screen, the cold-storage worked example, the IF–THEN rule item, and Borana, Hawassa, Addis Ababa, Debre Zeit and Jimma examples are added and marked.
